findings.source_quote: Ἁλῶν αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα συμμετασχεῖν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε
findings.english_quote: Halōn him when he comes, and make him partake with you.
findings.issue: Ἁλῶν has a defensible reading as the genitive plural of ἅλς, ‘salt’, governed by συμμετασχεῖν. The draft leaves this surviving lexical content untranslated and incorrectly declares the construction indefensible. Its proposed ἑλόντες unnecessarily replaces the verified printed reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Translate along the lines of ‘When he arrives, have him share salt with you.’ Explain the genitive construction and the shared-salt image in the note. Remove the assertion that source correction is necessary and distinguish any conjecture from the supplied reading. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.english_quote: I was afraid of the .........stō to disclose this.
findings.issue: The nine-dot gap and surviving ending are retained, but the accompanying note incorrectly treats τὸν and στω as necessarily belonging to one construction requiring agreement. The unavailable interval could contain several words. Moreover, the surviving στω does not securely establish a dative. Neither replacement of τὸν by τῷ nor identification of the fragment as Faustus is established.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the nine dots and identify στω as an incomplete surviving fragment. Explain that the gap prevents determination of the relationships among the accusative article, the fragment, and the infinitive. Remove the assertion of a demonstrated case mismatch and do not present the proposed τῷ [Φαύ]στῳ as necessary correction.

findings.source_quote: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ καιρὸν ἡμῖν ὁ Σίμων ἐδίδου πρὸς τὸ ἰδιάζειν .......... μῶν αὐτῷ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ Σίμωνος κακὴν ἐφάνη βουλήν
findings.english_quote: But Simon did not even give us time to confer privately..........mōn; to him Simon’s evil counsel appeared.
findings.issue: The ten-dot marker and μῶν are preserved, but the post-gap English presents τὴν ... βουλήν as an ordinary subject of ‘appeared’. The print instead has an accusative phrase with ἐφάνη. The note acknowledges that the connection is unresolved while the main text supplies a settled construction without explaining why that construction is defensible.
findings.suggested_revision: Represent the post-gap wording as explicitly disconnected translation fragments, preserving the ten dots and μῶν, and disclose the accusative phrase and the finite verb. Alternatively, justify a contextual rendering as anacoluthic syntax without claiming recovery of the missing connection. Do not silently substitute a nominative reading or characterize the verified print as an OCR error.

findings.source_quote: ἐναλειψάμενος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Σίμωνος ὢν προδιηγησάμην
findings.english_quote: since I was anointed by Simon himself—ōn, as I related beforehand
findings.issue: A nominative participle can accompany a first-person verb and agree with ἐγώ; the note's blanket claim that ὢν cannot form a defensible construction is incorrect. It can also be considered with ἐναλειψάμενος, ‘being one who has been anointed’. The draft leaves the complete word transliterated while introducing ‘as’, effectively using its proposed ὡς correction.
findings.suggested_revision: Translate the supplied ὢν rather than replacing it with comparative ὡς. A candidate for fresh review is ‘being one who has been anointed by Simon himself—I gave an account beforehand—so that ...’. Document the participial attachment and the parenthetical treatment of προδιηγησάμην as interpretations, retaining material alternatives. Remove the unsupported claim that manuscript correction is required.

findings.issue: Only μετα survives before the eight-dot gap. ‘Change’ supplies a completed noun whose identity and meaning are unavailable. The note says no completion has been supplied, but the main text does supply one. The dots therefore do not faithfully expose the interruption within the word.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain an explicitly identified incomplete fragment, such as ‘publicly proclaim your own [surviving fragment: μετα]........’. Explain that the noun's completion is unavailable and that no restoration has been supplied. Do not select ‘change’, ‘reorientation’, or another completed noun without evidence for the missing wording.

findings.source_quote: ὁμολογῶ ἀδίκως καταψεύ ........ ἔστι πλάνος, οὐ μιαιφόνος, οὐ γόης
findings.english_quote: I confess that I unjustly spoke falsely........ He is not a deceiver, not a murderer, not a sorcerer
findings.issue: The surviving wording has ἔστι πλάνος, not οὐκ ἔστι πλάνος. The draft supplies ‘not’ before ‘a deceiver’, apparently restoring a negation from the preceding lacuna. This unsupported completion reverses the surviving clause and is not disclosed in the note.
findings.suggested_revision: Preserve the surviving non-negated fragment, for example ‘........ is a deceiver, not a murderer, not a sorcerer’. Explain that any preceding qualification or negation is unavailable within the eight-dot gap and has not been restored. Also retain καταψεύ as an incomplete verbal form rather than claiming its missing completion has been recovered.

findings.source_quote: αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ὁ τοῦ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μίσους αἴτιος αὐτῷ γεγονώς
findings.english_quote: I myself became the cause of your hatred toward him
findings.issue: The Greek describes τοῦ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μίσους and separately supplies the dative αὐτῷ. The English resolves this as the listeners' hatred directed toward Peter without documenting the construction. A contextual reading involving hatred brought upon him among the listeners is defensible, but the directional alternative ‘hatred toward you’ is material and remains undisclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the draft explicitly with ‘I myself, who brought upon him the hatred among you’. If retaining the contextual reading, explain πρὸς ὑμᾶς as locating the hatred among or in relation to the listeners and αὐτῷ as marking the affected person. Preserve the alternative directional reading and its uncertain relationship to αὐτῷ in a note.

findings.source_quote: ἔξεστι γὰρ ἴσως μετανοίᾳ ἀπολῦσαι τὰ προπεπραγμένα μοι ἁμαρτήματα
findings.english_quote: Perhaps it is possible through reorientation to put away the sins previously committed by me.
findings.issue: The explanatory γὰρ is omitted. ‘Reorientation’ itself is contextually supported and does not require an added destination.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the connection: ‘For perhaps it is possible through reorientation to put away the sins previously committed by me.’

findings.english_quote: whom I love no less than you do.
findings.issue: The supplied comparison can mean either ‘whom I love no less than you love him’ or ‘whom I love no less than I love you’. The draft selects the former by adding ‘do’, but no note preserves the alternative or explains the contextual choice.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the contextual rendering only with a note giving both comparisons and explaining why Annoubion's reassurance about her husband favors comparing their respective love for him. Alternatively, use an English comparison that leaves the ellipsis unresolved.

findings.english_quote: And I myself will be with him.........
findings.issue: The print preserves only συμ before nine dots. That prefix does not establish a future verb or a promise of accompaniment; it could belong to compounds expressing sympathy, assistance, agreement, or other relationships. The draft invents a complete future predicate and places the gap after it. The note's claim that only a general sense has been supplied does not justify those additions.
findings.suggested_revision: Render καὶ αὐτὸς and preserve αὐτῷ as a dative whose relationship depends on the missing verb. Retain συμ as an explicitly identified incomplete prefix followed by exactly nine dots. State that the verb, tense, and resulting claim are unavailable and no restoration has been supplied. The block concerns the invented predicate, not the existence of a confirmed printed lacuna.
